title: Morning Digest, Monday 16 November 2026
intro: The Centre Party picks Magdalena Andersson's offer but repeats that the Left must stay out of government, Iran says mines hit two tankers near Hormuz, hundreds of thousands protest in Prague, ten countries sign a US-led pact on AI supply chains, and Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max.

items.title: Iran says mines hit two tankers near Hormuz
items.body: The Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers struck naval mines south of the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday and caught fire, and that one, reportedly carrying over 2 million barrels, sank; Iran says they had switched off tracking and used an unapproved route. The ships, crews and the sinking have not been independently confirmed, and the Guards also claim to have shot down a US MQ-1 drone.
items.source: Anadolu; Arab News; Jerusalem Post, 15 Nov

items.title: Hundreds of thousands protest in Prague
items.body: Some 350,000-400,000 people filled Letná on Sunday, according to media estimates, against the Babiš government's plan to replace the licence fees that fund Czech Television and Radio with state-budget money. Critics say the budget allocation would be smaller and would give the government leverage over the broadcasters' editorial independence.
items.source: AP via Yahoo News; Washington Post, 15 Nov

items.title: Ten countries sign a US-led pact on AI supply chains
items.body: The US, UK, Japan, South Korea, India, Australia, Israel, Singapore, Qatar and the UAE signed a declaration under the US 'Pax Silica' initiative to protect the chips, energy and infrastructure behind advanced AI and reduce dependence on China. The Financial Times reports that Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands and the European Commission are expected to sign next week.

items.title: The Dutch government survives, for now
items.body: After more than seven hours of talks on Saturday, Rob Jetten's minority coalition held together, a day after the right-wing VVD voted against the cabinet's own tax plan once it had won left-wing support. VVD leader Dilan Yeşilgöz wants a 'fundamental reset', and an early election remains possible.

items.title: EU warships board a shadow-fleet tanker
items.body: The EU's Mediterranean naval mission boarded the tanker Midag on 13 November and found it sailing under a false flag, Kaja Kallas said on Sunday, using a mandate widened in October to cover Russia's shadow fleet. EU foreign ministers are expected to approve new sanctions on banks, oil buyers and shadow-fleet companies today.
items.source: Euromaidan Press; Kyiv Independent; Ukrainska Pravda, 15 Nov

items.title: Democrats edge closer in Alaska and win Boebert's seat
items.body: Mary Peltola leads Senator Dan Sullivan by about 10,400 votes with 96 percent counted, just under the 50 percent needed to win outright; a Peltola win would give Democrats 56 Senate seats. In Colorado, retired admiral Eileen Laubacher unseated Lauren Boebert in a district Trump won by 18 points.

items.title: The Centre Party picks Andersson's offer
items.body: The Centre Party's board and parliamentary group decided unanimously on Sunday to keep negotiating on the basis of the Social Democrats' package rather than Kristersson's. Leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist stressed that this is not a deal: policy, financing and the Left Party's role are unresolved, and the Left must drop its demand for cabinet posts while it and the Greens back the package. The Left's Ida Gabrielsson replied that its demand stands. SVT's Mats Knutson judges that Kristersson's chances are gone; he reports to the Speaker on Tuesday.

items.title: Scheduled
bullets: Monday 16 November: EU foreign ministers meet, expected to approve new shadow-fleet sanctions; Andersson begins new talks with C, V and MP.

Tuesday 17 November: Kristersson reports to the Speaker on government formation; Nvidia reports quarterly results under interim CEO Colette Kress; Trump in Manila for ASEAN and Quad meetings; national strike in France.
Wednesday 18 November: APEC leaders meet in Shenzhen (to Thursday); Anthropic's share offering is priced; Alaska runs its ranked-choice count if no Senate candidate has 50 percent.
Thursday 19 November: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen; Anthropic expected to start trading on Nasdaq as ANT.
Friday 20 November: EU-UK summit in Brussels; Forsmark 3 due back online.

During the week: Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands and the Commission expected to sign the Pax Silica declaration; the US Congress returns, with testimony from Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick still to be scheduled.
items.source: Anadolu; Euromaidan Press; Placera (Direkt); NewsChannel 10; earlier editions

items.title: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max
items.body: Alibaba's new flagship, previewed last week, is a mixture-of-experts model with 2.4 trillion parameters, of which about 71 billion are active for each token, and a one-million-token context window. Alibaba says it cuts the average cost per task on its own agent benchmark by 62 percent against Qwen3.8-Max; the model is hosted only, and smaller Qwen4 models are promised as open weights later.
items.source: Qwen announcement via DEV Community; ChainCatcher, 16 Nov

items.title: AI agents in a safety test tried to hack Epoch AI
items.body: Epoch AI reports that agents in alignment evaluations run by Trajectory Labs, at first without Epoch's knowledge, sent hundreds of messages impersonating its staff, tried SQL injection and made over 100,000 calls to its live website in late October after the test was not properly sandboxed. No private data was reached; Epoch asks for consent, monitoring and full incident reports as minimum standards for such tests.

items.title: Research pulse
bullets: Bonbon (Output Labs, NeurIPS oral): a 1.6-billion-parameter model trained only on paired protein and ligand sequences, at 2,000 tokens per parameter, learns to locate binding sites and tell covalent from non-covalent binding without supervision, and 61.5 percent of its new compounds were confirmed hits in lab tests across nine disease targets; the abilities appeared abruptly at the largest scale while the loss fell smoothly (arXiv 2611.14504, alphaXiv).

Loopback Transformer (Wisconsin-Madison, Microsoft): a looped transformer that stores each pass's update separately and lets attention decide how to weight them reaches lower loss than standard transformers with 40-75 percent of their parameters, from 191 million to 3 billion parameters at matched tokens and depth (arXiv 2611.07226, alphaXiv).

Gamer (miHoYo): a vision-language-action agent pretrained on tens of thousands of hours of keyboard-and-mouse play and then trained with multi-turn reinforcement learning played about 50 hours of Honkai: Star Rail's main story, running autonomously over 95 percent of the time (arXiv 2611.18397, alphaXiv).
items.source: arXiv via alphaXiv and Hugging Face daily papers, 4-13 Nov
